answer: A timed sand watch admits a key. The applicant locks 13.9 POA and sets a 9-byte peg on one licensed dune crest, valid only in the 180-second window when a published comet path crosses zenith. Two unaffiliated wardens from distinct grid squares countersign peg and path within 70 seconds. Auditors recompute the crest ID from the epoch seed and check the one-crest cap plus timestamps. A 4,200-key farm needs 58,380 POA and 4,200 unshared crests in that window. A late mark, a second peg on the same crest, or a shared warden burns 68% of the lock and benches those wardens for nine epochs.
